# local Git actions and the Purrage action model
Tags: integrate-purrage
Status: Needs Test (approved and built on 2026-11-19; nine tasks done, three wait for the user's test; see doc-76). Part 3 of 5 in the Purrage integration.
Tasks: TASK-188, TASK-162, TASK-163, TASK-164, TASK-165, TASK-166, TASK-167, TASK-168, TASK-169, TASK-170, TASK-184, TASK-185.
## Why
The read-only backend (part 2) lets Ops show a local repository. It cannot change one. Ops Changes
needs its existing actions on the local backend, and the future Purrage mode needs Purrage's proven
whole-file actions: track, untrack, ignore and delete.
Purrage's action layer is worth reusing because it already solves the hard parts:
- optimistic row moves before git runs, with a failure restoring only that action's rows
- a serialized action queue, so two clicks cannot fight over the index
- an action that is still pending prevents a stale `git status` from flickering the list back
- every result carries the action, origin, command and parameters, so the console and notices can
say what happened
- the ignore rules know the difference between a root `.gitignore`, a folder `.gitignore`, the local
exclude file and the global ignore file, and handle nested repositories
Ops' `Changes` state already does part of this. A file stage or unstage moves the rows locally
before the backend answers (`act(..., optimistic:)`, `_moveLocally` in `lib/state/changes.dart`),
and a `_pending` count keeps a refresh from flipping the move back while an action runs. Hunk
actions are not optimistic, because only git knows the shifted line numbers.
What Ops lacks is the rest of Purrage's discipline: actions are not queued (two clicks run side by
side), a failed move is put back only by the full refresh after every action, not by restoring that
action's own rows, and the result is an error string rather than a record of the action, origin,
command and parameters. The local backend needs the same action discipline on both sides.
## The idea
Bring Purrage's action model into Ops as shared state logic, not as a second app: one status store
and one action queue per repository, under two thin mode states (Changes, and the Add and Ignore
mode), each owning only its cursor, selection and filter.
Local implementations of the existing Ops actions:
- stage, unstage and discard whole files
- stage, unstage and discard hunks
- commit, checkout, merge and rebase
- the same error text and command reporting Ops already shows
The Add and Ignore mode's actions (the Purrage mode's final name), built on the same machinery:
- track (stage a whole file), untrack (`git rm --cached`, never deleting from disk)
- ignore, with the rules engine, ignore targets, already-ignored checks and nested-repository guards
- delete through the trash, with the row leaving the list first
- file manager operations and hidden-file repair where the local platform needs it; these are
general Ops services any mode can call (Tasks, Repos), not part of the mode
The action result type, notices and Log entries are shared. The mode's state is built here and
testable without widgets; its view arrives in part 5. Ops Changes can use the local actions
immediately.
Commit stays in Ops Changes only. Purrage's commit bar (`lib/ui/commit_bar.dart`) is not ported.
## Scope
- Port Purrage's `Changes` action queue, optimistic row changes, `ActionResult` and failure/notice
reporting into Ops' state layer.
- Port the ignore rules and ignore-match parsing from Purrage.
- Implement local `stage`/`unstage`/`discard`, file and hunk variants, commit, checkout, merge and
rebase.
- Add the Purrage mode state: status rows, selection, filter, track/untrack/ignore/delete.
- Port the file manager, trash and hidden-write handling needed by those actions.
- Keep the Neovim backend's action behaviour unchanged.
## Out of scope
- The Purrage mode view, list widgets, ignore pane or dialog. That is part 5.
- The project crawler. That is part 4.
- Reworking Ops' diff view or commit bar beyond wiring them to the local backend.
- Changing the Neovim backend's merge-conflict worktree; it can stay there until later.
## Done when
- A local repository can stage, unstage, discard, commit, checkout, merge and rebase from Ops.
- Track, untrack, ignore and delete work from the state layer and are covered by tests.
- An action failure restores only its own rows and produces the same kind of report Ops already
shows.
- No Purrage view is needed to exercise the actions; tests drive the state objects.
## Decided (2026-11-19, the user)
| question | answer |
| State shape | **two thin mode states over a shared core**: one status store and one action queue per repository; the core's interface is designed first (Claude) and the port builds on it |
| Commit bar | **dropped**: commit only in Changes |
| File manager, trash, hidden write | **general Ops services**, behind the process seams |
| Notices and console | Purrage's **notice bar replaces the snackbar**, keeping the Details button and staying open while hovered; the Console is ported as the **Log** mode |
| Backend calls no part owned | Tasks file writes (TASK-184) and local jobs (TASK-185) are part 3; `dirs`/`cd` become part 4 hints; the merge-conflict worktree stays on Neovim for now |
## Open questions
None left for this part.
# backend seam for a second repository backend
Tags: integrate-purrage
Status: Needs Test (approved and built on 2026-11-19; the task waits for the user's test; see doc-76). Part 1 of 5 in the Purrage integration.
Tasks: TASK-154.
## Why
Ops reaches the repository only through `Backend` in `lib/backend/backend.dart`: one concrete class
that owns the Neovim RPC connection, the relay plugin calls and the event stream. Every mode depends
on it. That is why the app cannot work without Neovim and the relay plugin, even though almost
everything it asks for is git, files or processes.
Ops already hides part of that: `ops.exe <directory>` starts a headless Neovim in the folder on a
free loopback port (`lib/state/nvim_launcher.dart`), and finds the relay checkout next to the app or
in `~/ws`. So the problem is not that the user has to start Neovim by hand. It is the dependency
itself: an `nvim` on the machine, a relay checkout the launcher can find, the start-up and RPC cost
of every call, and an editor process kept alive for work that needs none.
The calls divide unevenly:
- 38 feature calls in `Backend`
- only three are editor calls: `open`, `show`, and the unused `getText`
- the rest are git, merge worktrees, file reads and writes, jobs, directories and `.nvimos` tracking;
of these, `dirs` (genja-startdirs, `v:oldfiles`), `cd` and `pluginRoot` read Neovim's own state
and need a local answer of their own
- `Session` attaches four event domains: `buffers`, `windows`, `git` and `jobs`; only `windows`
(the cursor), `git` (refresh hints) and `jobs` are used, `buffers` is ignored, and `diagnostics`
is not attached
A second backend needs a seam, not a rewrite of the modes.
## The idea
Split today's `Backend` into two pieces:
- `RepoBackend` — the repository operations the modes need: repository info, branches, log, diff,
status, stage/discard, commit, checkout/merge/rebase, file list/read/write, jobs, tracking
- `EditorSession` — optional editor operations: open a file at a line, show a revision read-only,
the live cursor and the current buffer text
The existing implementation becomes `NvimBackend`, wrapping the same relay calls and event stream.
It is still the only implementation at the end of this proposal; nothing user-visible changes.
`Session` holds a `RepoBackend` and an optional `EditorSession`. UI that needs an editor checks for
the capability and hides or disables the editor-only parts when it is absent. The Connect screen is
not changed yet.
## Scope
- Extract the interface from the current class; keep the models in `lib/backend/models.dart`.
- Keep `NvimBackend` behaviour identical, including the handshake, API version, event ordering and
resync.
- Express the optional editor capability so the mode code does not ask `session.backend` for
`open`/`show` when there is no editor.
- Keep the `Session.run((b) => ...)` shape the state classes already use.
## Out of scope
- Any local implementation; that is part 2.
- Any change to the Connect screen, the mode rail or the UI.
- Removing Neovim. The Neovim backend stays for local and remote use throughout the programme.
## Done when
- The app behaves exactly as before, against the same relay plugin.
- The existing tests pass without changes to their expectations.
- No mode calls the concrete RPC class directly.
## Decided (2026-11-19, the user)
| question | answer |
| Interfaces | **two**: `RepoBackend`, and an `EditorSession` that is null without an editor, so the compiler stops a mode calling `open`/`show` unchecked; `NvimBackend` implements both |
| Event stream | **split by owner**: `RepoBackend` emits git hints and jobs, `EditorSession` emits the cursor; `NvimBackend` keeps one RPC stream with seq and resync underneath |
| Status bar without an editor | **nothing**: the cursor area is simply absent, no badge and no button |
## Open questions
None left for this part.
# local Git backend, read-only
Tags: integrate-purrage
Status: Needs Test (approved and built on 2026-11-19; four tasks done, four wait for the user's test; see doc-76). Part 2 of 5 in the Purrage integration.
Tasks: TASK-155, TASK-156, TASK-157, TASK-158, TASK-159, TASK-160, TASK-161, TASK-186.
## Why
Ops cannot show a repository without Neovim. A local folder should open in the app, the Pull request
and Changes views should read it, and the Tasks view should read its planning files, with no editor
running at all.
Purrage already has a working local Git layer: repository discovery, a careful `git status
--porcelain=v1 -z` parser, branches, commits, `.gitignore` handling, file reads and writes, and
Windows-specific path handling. It is the part worth taking. Ops should not grow a second local git
implementation next to it.
The goal is not to merge Purrage's app into Ops. It is to reuse Purrage's local layer behind the
backend seam from part 1, as `LocalBackend`.
## The idea
`LocalBackend` implements `RepoBackend` directly:
- repository discovery and open from a folder (`Repo.open`, `GitDir.fromExisting` or an equivalent)
- `git status --porcelain=v1 -z --untracked-files=all --find-renames`, decoded as UTF-8 and parsed
into Ops' `Status` model
- branches, log and diff, ported from relay's `nvimos.git` commands into the local backend
- file list and read, from the filesystem
- `.nvimos` tracking parsing, without a Neovim buffer in between
- no editor capability; `EditorSession` is absent
The starting path is a folder. The Connect screen becomes a list of recent folders and Neovim
addresses, each remembering its backend; a folder entry creates a `LocalBackend` and the modes run
against it.
`ops.exe <directory>` exists already and today starts a headless Neovim in that folder
(`lib/main.dart`, `lib/state/nvim_launcher.dart`). It changes meaning: a directory opens a
`LocalBackend` right away, even while the local backend is still read-only. An address
(`127.0.0.1:port`) still selects Neovim.
The local backend watches the repository itself, since there is no relay to send git hints: one
debounced file watcher on the worktree and on `.git` (`index`, `HEAD`, `refs/`, `packed-refs`),
raising the same git change signal the Neovim backend raises. The History mode's refs watcher is the
same watcher, not a second one.
The app-facing models stay Ops' models. Purrage's `StatusRow` and `Section` are not allowed to become
a second truth: its parser feeds Ops' `Status`, `Branches`, `Commit`, `DiffFile` and `Hunk`.
## Scope
- Add the `git` package dependency (Purrage uses it) or an equivalent process layer; keep Purrage's
UTF-8 status decoding and argument batching.
- Port `Repo`, `GitRepo`, the status parser, `paths.dart` and the `.nvimos` tracking parser.
- Implement the read-only half of `RepoBackend`: branches, log, diff, status, file list/read.
- Port relay's `diffparse.lua` to Dart line by line, reusing relay's cases as fixtures.
- Add the repository watcher (shared with the History mode).
- Add the recent-entries Connect screen and backend selection in `Session`.
- Make Pull request, Changes and Tasks load from a local repository.
- Hide “Open in Neovim”, the live cursor and other editor-only UI when there is no editor.
- Keep the Neovim backend working exactly as before.
## Out of scope
- Any mutation: no stage, discard, commit, checkout or merge. That is part 3.
- The Purrage mode or any Purrage view. That is part 5.
- The project crawler and Directories. That is part 4.
- Merge-conflict worktrees. They stay on the Neovim backend, or move later.
- Removing relay or the Neovim backend.
## Done when
- A local folder opens with no Neovim running and looks like a normal Ops session.
- Pull request, Changes and Tasks read the local repository.
- The same folder still works through the Neovim backend, and the two paths agree on the models.
- No editor-only control is shown in local mode.
- The local backend is testable with a temporary repository and the process/file seams, without a
headless Neovim.
## Decided (2026-11-19, the user)
| question | answer |
| Change hints | **watch from the start**: one debounced watcher on the worktree and `.git`, shared with History; no timer |
| Diff parsing | **port `diffparse.lua`** line by line, relay's cases as fixtures, plus a parity test against the Neovim backend |
| `ops.exe <directory>` | **local right away**; an address still selects Neovim |
| Connect screen | **a recent list** of folders and addresses, each remembering its backend |
## Open questions
None left for this part.
# the Purrage mode and the remaining Purrage UI
Tags: integrate-purrage

Status: Needs Test (approved and built on 2026-11-19; two tasks done, nine wait for the user's test; the Ignore panes are reworked in `ops-ignore-pane`; see doc-76). Part 5 of 5 in the Purrage integration.
Tasks: TASK-175, TASK-176, TASK-177, TASK-178, TASK-179, TASK-180, TASK-181, TASK-182, TASK-183, TASK-187, TASK-189.
## Why
Parts 1 to 4 give Ops a local backend, local actions, the Purrage action model, and project
discovery. None of it is visible yet. This part turns the Purrage functionality into a mode inside
Ops and finishes the UI merge.
Ops remains the leading app: its shell, mode rail, theme, key contract, Pull request, Changes and
Tasks views stay. Purrage contributes the file-triage workflow, its views and its small tools. It is
not a second app inside the window.
## The idea
The final mode rail, numbered Alt+1 … Alt+9 in this order (History comes from the
`history-mode` proposal):
1. **Pull request** — Ops, unchanged
2. **Changes** — Ops' diff, hunks, staged list and commit; now backed by either backend
3. **Add and Ignore** — the whole-file mode from Purrage: a status list, add, untrack, ignore,
delete, with the preview pane
4. **History** — the stacked-branches view
5. **Tasks** — Ops, unchanged
6. **Repos** — the crawler from part 4 (the current Directories mode, widened, Browse folded in)
7. **Settings** — from Purrage, for editors, terminals, scan depth and prefs
8. **Log** — Purrage's Console, renamed: the action and scan reports
9. **Help** — merged key tables
The overlapping Changes views are resolved by purpose, not by choosing one:
- Ops Changes stays the diff and hunk mode, with checkout, merge/rebase and commit.
- Add and Ignore is the fast whole-file triage list: add, untrack, ignore, delete, with the
optimistic rows and the ignore pane. It is what Purrage was for.
- Both are thin states over one status store and action queue.
- Commit is only in Changes; Purrage's commit bar is not ported.
Purrage's notice bar replaces Ops' snackbar in every mode. It keeps Ops' Details button (the
selectable trace) and stays open while the mouse is over it.
The UI sources:
- Purrage's file list, row sections, selection model and ignore pane/dialog become the Add and
Ignore view, restyled to Ops' theme and keys.
- Purrage's Browse view is folded into the Repos view over the crawler state.
- Purrage's Settings view, editor detection and terminal launcher are ported, with Ops' `Prefs`
storage.
- Purrage's Console view and scan/action reports are ported as the Log mode.
- Purrage's preview pane and adapters (text, image, PDF through `pdfrx`) are ported into the Add

- Purrage's widgets and theme tokens are merged into Ops' existing ones; each duplicate is decided
once, by the user, in the widget table of `backlog/docs/doc-76`, and every mode follows.
The Purrage repository is frozen from stage 0 (bug fixes only) and archived after TASK-183.

- Port the ignore pane and ignore dialog.
- Build the Repos view over the part 4 state, with Browse folded in.
- Port Settings, including editor detection, terminal choice, folder opener, scan depth and prefs.
- Port Console as Log, with the action/scan report formatting.
- Replace the snackbar with Purrage's notice bar (Details button, open while hovered).
- Port the preview pane into the Add and Ignore mode.

## Out of scope

# project discovery from a directory crawler
Tags: integrate-purrage
Status: Needs Test (approved and built on 2026-11-19; three tasks done, one waits for the user's test; see doc-76). Part 4 of 5 in the Purrage integration.
Tasks: TASK-171, TASK-172, TASK-173, TASK-174.
## Why
Ops' Directories mode is built from the genja-startdirs plugin: the backend asks the plugin for its
frecency list, or falls back to the directories of Neovim's recent files. That is useful, but it is a
list of hints, not a map of the repositories on the machine. A fresh folder, a checkout the plugin
has never seen, or a machine without the plugin produces a thin or empty list.
Purrage's Browse mode already has the better foundation: it walks a starting directory, recognises a
repository by its `.git` (folder or file), skips the trees that should never be walked, records what
it scanned, and lists the repositories it found. It does not need a plugin, and it works with no
editor running.
## The idea
Make the directory crawler the source of truth for project discovery, and demote start-dirs to a
hint source.
The crawler:
- starts from the connected Neovim's working directory; with no Neovim, from the last folder the
user browsed, or home on a first run
- walks to a configurable depth, never following links
- treats a directory with a `.git` as a repository and does not walk into that repository's own
subfolders looking for more
- has a skip list for build, cache and system trees, with a shallower rule for `AppData`
- reports visited, found, skipped, elapsed and the slowest/widest directories, for the console
- can be stopped and replaced by a newer scan
The hints:
- genja-startdirs' frecency list, when a Neovim backend is connected
- Neovim's recent-file directories as the fallback, as today
- the user's own recent projects from `Prefs` when no Neovim is connected
- the currently connected repository and the active directory, shown first
Hints do not replace the walk. They seed it, order its results, and put the likely repositories at
the top. A hint that is not a repository, or no longer exists, is shown greyed with a Remove button;
it is never dropped behind the user's back.
The existing Directories mode becomes the **Repos** mode, and its state a view over the crawler plus
the hints. Purrage's Browse view is folded into it: one view, not two. “Active Directory”,
“Open project” and the picker behaviour stay as they are.
## Scope
- Port Purrage's `RepoBrowser` and its scan report, skip list and depth setting.
- Add a hint layer over it: start-dirs/oldfiles when connected, `Prefs` when not, and the active
repository.
- Merge the source of the Directories list: crawl results first, hints as ordering and seed.
- Keep the crawler in the state layer, testable with a fake directory lister.
- Keep the Neovim backend able to supply hints; it is not required for the crawl.
## Out of scope
- The Browse or Directories view. The UI is part 5.
- The local git backend and actions; parts 2 and 3.
- Fetching, cloning or creating repositories.
- Watching the filesystem for new repositories; a rescan is enough for now.
## Done when
- The crawler finds repositories under a folder with no Neovim running.
- Start-dirs and oldfiles order or seed the list when connected, but are not required.
- The active and connected repositories appear first.
- The Directories state can be driven by a fake lister in tests.
- A scan reports what it did, and a second scan replaces a running one cleanly.
## Decided (2026-11-19, the user)
| question | answer |
| Mode name | **Repos** |
| Browse view | **folded into Repos**: one view |
| Stale hint | **shown greyed** with a Remove button |
| Start directory | **the Neovim cwd** when connected; otherwise the last folder used, home on a first run |
## Open questions
None left for this part.
# time relay requests
Status: To Do (backlog TASK-149)
## Why
Ops feels slow in places, and I don't know yet where the time goes. Ops already measures its own
side: every backend call is timed as `rpc <module>.<fn>` and summarized per session into
`%APPDATA%\nvimos\ui-timing.json`. That number is the whole round trip: msgpack over the socket,
Neovim getting round to the request, the Lua, the git it runs, and the way back. It says
`changes.refresh` takes 650 ms, but not whether that is git, the Lua around it, or waiting in line.
The relay should measure its own side the same way: how long each request takes inside Neovim, and
how much of that is git. Put next to Ops's file, the difference is the transport and the queue.
With both, I can decide what to optimize from numbers instead of guesses.
## The idea
The relay times every request it serves. A request is one API endpoint, the `<module>.<fn>` that Ops
calls through `nvim_exec_lua` (`nvimos.attach`, `nvimos.git.status`, `nvimos.files.diff`, ...), not
the internal functions those call. The names are the same as Ops's `rpc` keys, so the two files can
be read side by side.
For each request it records the time from entry to return, whether it raised an error, and how much
of that time was spent in git commands (every git call goes through `repo.run`, so one hook there
covers them all). It keeps the raw times in memory for the session, which is the life of the Neovim
process.
When Neovim exits (`VimLeavePre`), the relay writes the session's summary into a stats file, and
every few minutes in between, so a crash loses little. The file keeps the last 30 sessions and
totals across them. It works quietly: no messages, no notifications, and a failure to write is
swallowed. Timing can be turned off with `NVIMOS_TIMING=0`, the same switch Ops uses; it is on by
default, since the relay has no release build.
The file lives in local app data, not the roaming one: `%LOCALAPPDATA%\nvimos\relay-timing.json` on
Windows, `~/.local/state/nvimos/relay-timing.json` elsewhere. Several Neovims may run at once; each
reads the file, adds its session, and writes it back in one go, so the last one to exit wins for
the totals, and no session is dropped as long as two don't exit in the same instant.
### What the file shows
Per session: when it started and ended, and per endpoint:
- `n`: how many calls
- `avg`, `p50`, `p95`, `max`: the call's time in ms
- `total`: all its calls together, in ms, which is what ranks the endpoints by cost
- `git`: the time in git, as `avg` and `total`
- `errors`: how many calls raised
Across the kept sessions (`totals`), per endpoint: the total count, the overall average, the worst
`p95` and `max`, the total time, and its share of all time spent serving requests. The totals are
sorted by total time, so the first entries are the ones to look at.
The format follows Ops's `ui-timing.json`, with the added `avg`, `total`, `git` and `errors`.
An endpoint that only starts work and returns (a job in `nvimos.jobs`) is timed to its return, not
to the job's end. The job's own run time is a later question.
## Impact
Relay (`nvimos/relay`): a new `lua/nvimos/timing.lua`. The public functions of the modules Ops calls
are wrapped once, when the module is loaded, so no endpoint knows about the timing; `repo.run` adds
its time to the request in progress. A `VimLeavePre` autocmd and a timer write the file. A test
calls a few endpoints and reads back the summary. The README names the file and the switch.
## ADDED Requirements
### Requirement: Every request is timed
The relay SHALL time every call Ops makes to a public function of its modules, keyed by
`<module>.<fn>`, from entry to return, with the time spent in git commands during the call and
whether it raised an error.
#### Scenario: A git request
- **WHEN** Ops calls `nvimos.git.status`
- **THEN** the session records one `nvimos.git.status` call with its time in ms and its git time
#### Scenario: A failing request
- **WHEN** a request raises an error
- **THEN** it is recorded with its time and counted under `errors`, and the error reaches Ops as before
### Requirement: Stats are written quietly when the session ends
The relay SHALL write the session's summary to `relay-timing.json` in the local app data folder
(`%LOCALAPPDATA%\nvimos\` on Windows) when Neovim exits and every few minutes before that, keeping
the last 30 sessions and totals across them. Writing SHALL show no message and a failure SHALL not
disturb Neovim.
#### Scenario: Neovim exits
- **WHEN** Neovim exits after serving requests
- **THEN** the file holds this session with, per endpoint, `n`, `avg`, `p50`, `p95`, `max`, `total`,
`git` and `errors`, and the totals are updated
#### Scenario: Ranking the slow parts
- **WHEN** the file is read
- **THEN** the totals list each endpoint with its count, average, worst p95, max, total time and share
of all request time, sorted by total time
#### Scenario: The folder can't be written
- **WHEN** the stats file can't be written
- **THEN** nothing is shown and Neovim exits normally
### Requirement: Timing can be turned off
The relay SHALL skip all timing when `NVIMOS_TIMING=0` is set, and time by default otherwise.
#### Scenario: Off
- **WHEN** Neovim starts with `NVIMOS_TIMING=0`
- **THEN** no request is timed and no file is written
# tasks from several sources
Status: Open proposal, not decided. Nothing is built for it yet.
## Why
Ops's Tasks mode reads two kinds of files today, and each has its own model in the code. A
Backlog.md task (`Task` in `lib/tasks/model.dart`) has front matter with an id, a status, a priority,
labels, dependencies and a milestone, and sections with checkboxes: Acceptance Criteria, Definition
of Done, Verify. An OpenSpec change (`Change`) has a proposal with a `Status:` line and a tasks.md
whose checkboxes are grouped into Build and Verify. The views, the auto status after a tick and the
planned Board mode each know both shapes and handle them separately.
That is fine for two sources that live in the same folder. It does not stretch to the next ones. A
team (see `team-planning`) keeps its work in GitHub issues or in Linear, not in markdown files next
to the code, and I want to see those in the same list, with the same filters, and change a status
from the same place. Adding a third and a fourth model to every view is the wrong way to get there.
So the goal is one task model in the UI, with sources behind it. The views show tasks; where a task
comes from is a detail of the source.
## The idea
A task is what the UI shows and edits: a title, a status, a priority, some labels, a body, and
checklists. A source (a provider) turns its own records into tasks and turns the user's edits back
into its own writes. Backlog.md is the first source and the reference: the model is shaped after
it, because it is what the Tasks mode already does well. OpenSpec tasks.md is the second, already
read today. GitHub issues and Linear are kept in mind now, so the model doesn't have to be broken
open again when they arrive, but they are not built in this change.
Each source says what it can do. Backlog.md can do everything: read, change the status and the
priority, tick a box, create a task. An OpenSpec tasks.md has no status of its own, only boxes. A
read-only GitHub source would show issues and offer nothing to edit. The UI hides or disables an
action the source can't do, instead of failing on it.
Status is the field that differs most between sources. Every source has its own names (Backlog.md's
To Do, In Progress, Needs Test, Done, Dropped; Linear's workflow states; GitHub's open and closed).
The UI keeps the source's name for display, and every status also maps to a small fixed set of
kinds, which is what filters, sorting, the Board's lanes and the auto status work with:
| kind        | Backlog.md (this repo) | OpenSpec tasks.md        | GitHub issue                 | Linear state type    |
| backlog     | -                      | -                        | -                            | backlog, triage      |
| todo        | To Do                  | no box ticked            | open                         | unstarted            |
| in progress | In Progress            | some boxes ticked        | open, with an "in progress" project field or label | started |
| review      | Needs Test             | Build ticked, Verify open | -                           | started (named review) |
| done        | Done                   | every box ticked         | closed (completed)           | completed            |
| dropped     | Dropped                | -                        | closed (not planned)         | canceled             |
The statuses a project uses stay in its own config (Backlog.md's `statuses` in
`backlog/config.yml`); only the mapping to a kind is new. A status with no mapping counts as todo.
Overlap is out of scope. The same work can show up twice, for example a Backlog.md task and the
GitHub issue it was copied from, or a change and the tasks that name it. This change does not merge
or hide duplicates; it only makes sure each task knows its source, so a later change can.
## Fields
The model, with Backlog.md as the reference. "Required" means every source must fill it.
| field        | required | Backlog.md            | OpenSpec tasks.md            | GitHub issue              | Linear issue               |
| source       | yes      | `backlog`             | `openspec`                   | `github`                  | `linear`                   |
| id           | yes      | `TASK-142`            | change id, plus box number   | `nvimos/ops#12`           | `OPS-12`                   |
| title        | yes      | `title`               | the box's text               | title                     | title                      |
| status       | yes      | `status`              | from the box marks           | state (+ state reason)    | workflow state             |
| status kind  | yes      | mapped                | mapped                       | mapped                    | the state's type           |
| priority     | no       | `priority` (high, medium, low) | -                   | a label or a project field | 0 to 4 (none, urgent, high, medium, low) |
| labels       | no       | `labels`              | -                            | labels                    | labels                     |
| assignees    | no       | `assignee`            | -                            | assignees                 | assignee (one)             |
| milestone    | no       | `milestone`           | -                            | milestone                 | project or cycle           |
| dependencies | no       | `dependencies`        | -                            | sub-issues, "blocked by"  | relations (blocks)         |
| parent       | no       | -                     | the change                   | parent issue              | parent issue               |
| order        | no       | `ordinal`             | line in tasks.md             | -                         | sort order                 |
| created      | no       | `created_date`        | file time                    | created at                | created at                 |
| updated      | no       | file time             | file time                    | updated at                | updated at                 |
| body         | no       | Description           | -                            | body (markdown)           | description (markdown)     |
| checklists   | no       | Acceptance Criteria, Definition of Done, Verify | the box itself | task lists in the body | -          |
| link         | yes      | the file path         | the file and line            | the issue URL             | the issue URL              |
| change       | no       | the OpenSpec change it names | the change            | -                         | -                          |
Priority is a small fixed scale too: none, low, medium, high, urgent. Backlog.md has the middle
three; Linear has all five; GitHub has none of its own, so a source config names the labels or the
project field that stand for it.
Checklists keep their marks (open, x, in progress, partly, will not do), as the Tasks mode already
shows them. A source without those marks shows open and x only.
## How it fits in Ops
Today `Workspace` (`lib/tasks/workspace.dart`) loads the planning folder and builds `Task` and
`Change` objects from the files. In this change:
- a `TaskSource` interface: list the tasks, watch for changes, and the edits it supports (set
status, set priority, tick a box, create), each returning an error string the way `edit()` does
now
- what a source can do, as flags the views read (`canSetStatus`, `canTick`, `canCreate`, ...)
- `BacklogSource` wraps today's `Task` parsing and edits; `OpenSpecSource` turns a change's tasks.md
boxes into tasks whose parent is the change
- the views (list, detail, filters, sorting) and the auto status after a tick work on the common
model; the change detail (proposal, specs, deltas) stays a change view
- the status-kind mapping for Backlog.md lives next to `statuses` in the planning config, with the
table above as the default
GitHub and Linear are only checked against the model on paper here: their fields fill the table
above without a new required field. Building them is a later change each, with its own questions
(auth, rate limits, offline, how often to fetch).
Today's link from a change to its task reads the first `TASK-n` on the proposal's `Status:` line
(`Change.taskId`). With changes split into several tasks (as `merge-beside-checkout` is now), the
link goes the other way too: a task names its change, and the change lists the tasks that name it.
## Open questions
- Is an OpenSpec box a task of its own, or only a checklist item of its change? As a task it gets a
status and shows in the list; as a checklist it stays as it is now.
- Where does the status-kind mapping for a GitHub repo or a Linear team live: in the planning config
of the repo that shows them, or in Ops's own settings?
- Do edits to a remote source (GitHub, Linear) go out at once, or are they queued and shown as
pending?
- Should the Tasks mode show the source as a column, a filter, or only an icon?
## Impact
Ops (`nvimos/ops`): `lib/tasks/model.dart`, `parse.dart`, `workspace.dart`, `auto_status.dart` and
the Tasks views move to the common model. The planned Board mode (`kanban-board-mode`) uses status
kinds for its lanes. No change to the files on disk: Backlog.md tasks and OpenSpec changes are read
and written as they are now.
# Tasks
Only if the proposal is accepted.

# team planning for 5-7 people
Status: To Do (backlog TASK-122)
## Why
The Tasks mode and the planning folder are built for one person: "Multiple users" is a non-goal of
the first version (`poc-nvim-backend/flutter-project-man.md`). A team of 5 to 7 sharing one planning
repo over git would hit these, worst first:
- duplicate task numbers: a new task takes the highest local number plus one, so two people who
create a task before pulling both get the same number; the file names differ by slug, git merges
both without a conflict, and two tasks share one id
- `index.tsv`: every status change writes a row in this one shared file, and edits to nearby rows
land in the same merge hunk; it repeats what the task headers already hold
- no sync: the app writes through Neovim buffers, `auto_commit` is off and nothing pulls or pushes
the planning repo, so each person's board is as old as their last manual pull
- the "file changed meanwhile" check in the edits only sees local changes, not a teammate's
- no ownership: `assignee` is written as `[]` and never shown or set, so two people can start the
same task without knowing
- task status edited on agent branches only shows on the board after the branch is merged
Editing the same task is the smallest of these: a status is one header line and checkboxes on
different lines merge cleanly.
## What Changes
- task ids that can't collide between clones, readable in a list (a short random or time-based
suffix, or the author's initials), the existing numbers kept as they are
- `index.tsv` generated from the task headers, or dropped; never edited by hand or by the app
- sync of the planning folder from the app: pull with rebase, commit the app's own edits, push;
a status that shows how far behind or ahead the planning repo is
- taking a task: assignee from `git config user.name`, status In Progress, committed and pushed
at once; a rejected push means someone was first, so the app pulls and shows who
- the assignee on the list row and in the detail panel; a "mine" filter
- task status always written in the planning repo on its default branch, never on a code branch
- a start for a teammate: the backend plugin on a stock Neovim, a clean planning repo without this
config's history
## Impact
- frontend: `lib/tasks/workspace.dart` (task ids, the index, sync, take), `lib/tasks/edits.dart`,
`lib/ui/tasks/` (assignee, "mine" filter, sync status), the keys in `PLAN.md`
- backend: git commands in the planning folder (`tracking.lua`), pull and push
- nvimos-meta: the task id format, `index.tsv`, `README.md`, the `planning` spec
## ADDED Requirements
### Requirement: Task ids don't collide
A new task SHALL get an id that no other clone of the planning repo can give at the same time.
#### Scenario: Two people create a task offline
- **WHEN** two clones each create a task before pulling, then both sync
- **THEN** the two tasks have different ids and the merge has no conflict
### Requirement: No shared file per status change
A status change SHALL write only the task's own files; `index.tsv`, if kept, is generated.
#### Scenario: Status changes on different tasks
- **WHEN** two people change the status of two different tasks and both sync
- **THEN** git merges both without a conflict
### Requirement: Sync from the app
The Tasks mode SHALL pull, commit its own edits and push the planning folder, and show how far it is
behind or ahead.
#### Scenario: A teammate moved a task
- **WHEN** a teammate pushed a status change
- **THEN** it shows on the board after one sync
### Requirement: Taking a task
Taking a task SHALL set its assignee and status In Progress and push at once; a rejected push means
someone else took it first.
#### Scenario: Two people take the same task
- **WHEN** two people take one task at about the same time
- **THEN** the second push is rejected, the app pulls and shows who has the task

- [ ] 1.2 generate `index.tsv` from the task headers, or drop it and update the scan tools

- [ ] 1.4 frontend: sync action and the ahead/behind status

# planning from a remote repo when there is no local checkout
Status: Open proposal, not decided. Nothing is built for it yet.
## Why
Some projects keep their planning in a separate repo: the Backlog.md tasks and the OpenSpec changes
live in a meta repo, and each code repo has a committed `.nvimos` file whose `tracking` line points
to a local checkout of it (`tracking = ../nvimos-meta/`). That works on my machine, where both
repos sit side by side. It does not work for anyone else.
Someone who downloads Ops and clones only the code repo opens it and sees an empty Tasks mode. The
`.nvimos` file names a folder that isn't there, and nothing tells them where the planning actually
lives or how to get it. To see what is in progress they would have to know that a meta repo exists,
find it, clone it next to the code repo under exactly the right name, and reopen. Nobody does that.
The first case is a demo: I want to show Ops to someone on their machine or a fresh one, clone the
code repo, open it, and have the Tasks mode full of real tasks right away. But it is also a plain
useful feature: a contributor who only works on the code still wants to see what is planned and
what is being worked on, without setting up a second repo they will never write to.
## The idea
The `.nvimos` file gets a second line that names the planning repo on GitHub, next to the local
path:
tracking = ../nvimos-meta/
tracking_remote = nvimos/meta
project = frontend
When Ops opens a repo, it looks for the planning in this order:
1. the local `tracking` folder, if it exists: the normal case, nothing changes
2. otherwise, if `tracking_remote` is set, a snapshot of that repo's `main`, which Ops fetches as an
archive and keeps in its own local state
3. otherwise, the repo root, as today
The snapshot is perishable. It lives in Ops's cache folder, not next to the code, nobody edits it,
and Ops may delete and fetch it again at any time. It is a read-only window on the planning as it
is on `main`: the tasks, their status, the OpenSpec changes, the progress of their boxes.
Because it is read-only, the Tasks mode shows it as such. A bar at the top says where the tasks come
from and how old the snapshot is ("snapshot of nvimos/meta main, fetched 12 minutes ago"), with a
Refresh button. Status changes, priority changes and ticking boxes are disabled with a tooltip that
says why: an edit to the snapshot would be lost on the next fetch and never reach the team. The bar
also offers to clone the planning repo to the `tracking` path for someone who does want to edit;
after the clone the local folder wins and the snapshot is no longer used.
Ops fetches the snapshot without being asked: the first time a repo with `tracking_remote` and no
local folder is opened, and again when it is opened later and the snapshot is older than an hour.
Opening never waits for the network: an existing snapshot shows at once and is replaced when the
new one arrives; with no snapshot yet, the Tasks mode shows a loading state. When the fetch fails
(offline, rate limit, a private repo without access) an old snapshot stays in use with its age in
the bar; with none, the Tasks mode says it could not fetch the planning and why, with a Retry.
## Use cases
**Showing Ops to someone.** I sit down at Kari's laptop, install Ops from the release page, and
clone `nvimos/ops`. I open it in Ops and switch to Tasks. For a second it says it is fetching the
planning from nvimos/meta, then the list fills: task 194 "ops PDF preview" in To Do, the ignore
panes in progress, the board change as a proposal. I click through them, open a change, show its
boxes. Nothing to configure. (The `tracking_remote` line and the snapshot do all of it.)
**A contributor who only codes.** Ola clones the frontend to fix a bug he found. He wants to know
whether someone is already on it. He opens the Tasks mode, filters on "frontend", and finds the
task, In Progress, with a branch name. He tries to change its priority and the control is greyed
out: "read-only snapshot of nvimos/meta; clone it to edit". He doesn't need to. (The read-only
snapshot and its bar.)
**Working offline.** On the train, Ola opens the repo again. The fetch fails; the bar says
"snapshot from yesterday 14:20, could not refresh: offline", and the tasks are there. (The old
snapshot stays until a new one arrives.)
**Becoming a planner.** Kari decides to help with the planning. She clicks "Clone to
../nvimos-meta/" in the bar. Ops clones the repo, the bar disappears, and her edits now go into
her checkout like mine do. The snapshot is deleted. (The local folder wins over the snapshot.)
## Technical notes
- `.nvimos` key
- `tracking_remote = <owner>/<repo>` for GitHub; a full `https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>` is
accepted too
- optional `tracking_ref = <branch>` for a branch other than `main`; the default is the repo's
`main`
- unknown keys are already ignored by today's reader, so old Ops versions are unaffected
- fetch
- `https://codeload.github.com/<owner>/<repo>/zip/refs/heads/<ref>` (what
`github.com/<owner>/<repo>/archive/refs/heads/<ref>.zip` redirects to); no API token for a
public repo
- a private repo: if `gh auth token` gives a token, send it as `Authorization: Bearer` to the API
zipball endpoint (`https://api.github.com/repos/<owner>/<repo>/zipball/<ref>`); otherwise the
failure message says the repo is private or missing and suggests cloning it
- keep the response's `ETag` and send `If-None-Match` on the next fetch, so an unchanged repo
costs a 304 and no download
- the first version only needs GitHub; the key's value is shaped so another host can be added
later
- where it lives
- `%LOCALAPPDATA%\nvimos\ops\tracking\<owner>\<repo>\<ref>\` with the extracted tree and a
`snapshot.json` (fetched at, ETag, commit sha from the archive's top folder name)
- extract into a new temp folder next to it, then swap the folders, so a crash mid-extract never
leaves a half snapshot in use
- it is a cache: deleting the folder is always safe
- the archive is untrusted data
- extract only what the Tasks mode reads: `backlog/` and `openspec/` (`.md`, `.yml`, `.yaml`)
- reject entries with `..`, absolute paths or links; cap the archive size and the file count
- nothing in it is run
- reading
- the snapshot folder is handed to the same task loader as a local tracking folder, with a
read-only flag on the `Tracking` (`lib/tasks/workspace.dart`)
- the workspace exposes the source (local folder or snapshot, its age, the last fetch error) for
the bar
- edit actions check the flag in the state class, not only in the widgets, so a key binding
can't write to the snapshot either
- with the relay backend, the backend's `tracking.lua` still resolves a local folder; the snapshot
is an Ops-side fallback used only when that resolves to nothing
- clone
- "Clone to <tracking>" runs `git clone https://github.com/<owner>/<repo> <tracking path>` and
reloads the workspace; the snapshot folder is removed afterwards
- tests
- a local zip served from a test HTTP server (no network in tests); the cache root goes through
`keepForCleanup`
- order of precedence, read-only edits refused, a 304 keeps the snapshot, a failed fetch keeps
the old snapshot, a hostile archive (`..`, a link) extracts nothing outside the folder
## Out of scope
- writing back to the remote (issues, pull requests to the meta repo from the snapshot)
- other hosts than GitHub
- planning repos that need more than `backlog/` and `openspec/`
## ADDED Requirements
### Requirement: Remote planning repo in .nvimos
The `.nvimos` file SHALL accept a `tracking_remote` key naming the planning repo on GitHub
(`owner/repo` or its URL), and an optional `tracking_ref` (default `main`).
#### Scenario: Old reader
- **WHEN** an Ops version without this change reads a `.nvimos` with `tracking_remote`
- **THEN** it ignores the key and behaves as before
### Requirement: Snapshot when there is no local checkout
When the local `tracking` folder does not exist and `tracking_remote` is set, Ops SHALL fetch an
archive of the remote ref into its cache folder and show the planning from it. A local `tracking`
folder SHALL always win over the snapshot.
#### Scenario: Fresh clone
- **WHEN** a repo whose `.nvimos` has `tracking_remote` is opened and the `tracking` folder is
missing
- **THEN** Ops fetches the snapshot without being asked and the Tasks mode shows its tasks and
changes
#### Scenario: Local checkout present
- **WHEN** the `tracking` folder exists
- **THEN** Ops reads it and fetches nothing
#### Scenario: Stale snapshot
- **WHEN** the repo is opened and the snapshot is older than an hour
- **THEN** the old snapshot shows at once and is replaced when the new fetch arrives
#### Scenario: Fetch fails
- **WHEN** the fetch fails
- **THEN** an existing snapshot stays in use with its age and the error in the Tasks bar; with no
snapshot the Tasks mode shows the error and a Retry
### Requirement: Snapshot is read-only
A snapshot SHALL NOT be edited. Status, priority and checkbox changes SHALL be refused by the state
and shown disabled with a tooltip that says why.
#### Scenario: Edit attempt
- **WHEN** the user tries to change a task's status in a snapshot, by click or key
- **THEN** nothing is written and the control says the tasks are a read-only snapshot
### Requirement: Archive is untrusted
Ops SHALL extract only `backlog/` and `openspec/` text files from the archive, SHALL NOT write
outside the snapshot folder, and SHALL NOT run anything from it.
#### Scenario: Hostile entry
- **WHEN** the archive holds an entry with `..`, an absolute path or a link
- **THEN** that entry is skipped and nothing is written outside the snapshot folder

# zen layouts by task
Status: Needs Test (backlog TASK-21)
## Why
One zen mode doesn't fit every job. Reading code or prose wants nothing but the text; working wants a
little UI (limited diagnostics, a line width marker); debugging wants all of it, with the debug panes
beside the code. Today z1 and z2 differ only in width and line numbers.
## What Changes
- z1: reading and prose, usable for anything: only the text, centred
- z2: some UI: limited diagnostics, a maximum line width marker
- z3: UI heavy: no zen float, maximized, numbers, all diagnostics, the debug UI as splits in the
current tab (outside z3 the debug UI keeps its own tab)
- z0: off, restores the window size, diagnostics and options from before
## Impact
- `lua/genja/map-plugin/zenmode.lua` (keys z0..z3), the dap UI setup (`lua/lazyp/langs/dap*.lua`)
- built on the config's `PR-zen` branch, not merged; test session in that branch's `todo-test/zen-modes.md`
- open: dap-ui or dap-view in z3; open the debug UI at once or on the first stop
## ADDED Requirements
### Requirement: Layout per task
The config SHALL offer one zen layout per kind of work, each on its own key.
#### Scenario: Reading
- **WHEN** the user presses z1
- **THEN** only the text shows, centred, without signs or diagnostics
#### Scenario: Debugging
- **WHEN** the user presses z3 during a debug session
- **THEN** the window is maximized with numbers and all diagnostics, and the debug panes open as splits beside it
### Requirement: Leaving restores
Leaving a zen layout SHALL restore the window size, diagnostics and options from before it.
#### Scenario: z0 after z2
- **WHEN** the user presses z0 in z2
- **THEN** the window size and the diagnostics limit are as they were before z2

# completion Specification
## Purpose
How completion behaves in buffers and on the command line.
## Requirements
### Requirement: blink.cmp completion
Completion SHALL come from blink.cmp, with the config's own sources built on one source builder.
#### Scenario: Insert mode
- **WHEN** the user types in a buffer with an LSP attached
- **THEN** the menu offers LSP, buffer-word and path items
### Requirement: Command-line completion like plain Vim
On the command line `<Up>`/`<Down>` SHALL recall history; the menu moves on `<M-j>`/`<M-k>`.
#### Scenario: History
- **WHEN** the user presses `<Up>` on an empty `:` line
- **THEN** the previous command is recalled, not a menu item
# languages Specification
## Purpose
How languages are added to and enabled in the config.
## Requirements
### Requirement: Adding a language is one documented step
Adding a language SHALL follow one checklist (`readme.add-a-language.md`): parsers, LSP, linters,
formatter, test runner, debug adapter, each in its lang module.
#### Scenario: A new language
- **WHEN** the user follows the checklist for a language
- **THEN** opening a file of that language gives highlighting, completion and diagnostics without other edits
### Requirement: Only the languages in use
Only languages a spec turns on SHALL be installed, with a conservative set of defaults.
#### Scenario: Unused language
- **WHEN** a language is not turned on in the spec
- **THEN** none of its servers or parsers are installed
# planning Specification
## Purpose
Where the config's plans, todos and finished work are kept, and in which format.
## Requirements
### Requirement: Planning lives in nvimos-meta
The config's todos, ideas and solved issues SHALL live in nvimos-meta, not in the config repo.
#### Scenario: A solved issue
- **WHEN** `/close-issues` closes an issue in the config
- **THEN** it writes a Backlog.md task in nvimos-meta and commits it there; the config gets no todo file
### Requirement: Backlog.md first, OpenSpec for design
Every item SHALL be a Backlog.md task; work that needs a proposal or specs also gets an OpenSpec change
that names its task (`Status: X (backlog TASK-n)`). No item is copied into both formats.
#### Scenario: A small fix
- **WHEN** a fix needs no design
- **THEN** it is a Backlog.md task only
#### Scenario: A change split into work items
- **WHEN** a change's work splits into several steps
- **THEN** each step is a Backlog.md task that names the change, with its hand checks under `## Verify`;
the change has no tasks.md, and its proposal's Status line names the tasks (the first one in the
parentheses)
